claims.text: The initial FeMnNiGeSi film is 200 nm thick.
The as-deposited film has an average nanocrystalline grain size of approximately 10 nm.
The as-deposited film has random crystallographic texture.
The film is patterned into ribbons on a nonmagnetic Si/SiO2 substrate.
The controlled intervention is annealing at 500 °C for 1 hour under flowing Ar.
Annealing at 500 °C for 1 hour will increase the average grain size from approximately 10 nm to approximately 50 nm.
The annealing treatment will reduce defect density.
Grain growth will reduce grain-boundary density.
Fewer grain-boundary constraints will enhance magnetoelastic coupling.
Fewer grain-boundary constraints will enable more coherent martensitic-austenitic interconversion at the nanoscale.
Enhanced magnetoelastic coupling and more coherent phase interconversion will increase the peak magnetic entropy change.
Enhanced magnetoelastic coupling and more coherent phase interconversion will reduce magnetic hysteresis width.
Annealing will produce at least a 20% increase in peak magnetic entropy change relative to the as-deposited film at a maximum applied field of 0.5 T.
Annealing will produce at least a 30% reduction in hysteresis-loop width relative to the as-deposited film at a maximum applied field of 0.5 T.
The as-deposited baseline peak magnetic entropy change is approximately 1.0 J kg^-1 K^-1 at a maximum applied field of 0.5 T.
The as-deposited baseline hysteresis width is approximately 0.12 T at a maximum applied field of 0.5 T.
The proposed operating window is 220–260 K, maximum applied field no greater than 0.5 T, and cycle frequency no greater than 1 Hz for 200 nm plates or ribbons.
Cycling at frequencies no greater than 1 Hz constitutes a heat-transfer-limited regime for this film geometry.
